observed: The tracking tolerance sigma is derived under two different kernels in two places. One set of the project's working notes states it is the sigma in a GAUSSIAN exp(-|v-v_cmd|^2/sigma^2); research/scripts/measure_tracking_noise.py derives it under a CAUCHY Phi(u)=1/(1+u^2), and the 3x rule's 0.900 floor score is Cauchy-specific. research/CORE_PLAN.md:162 uses the Gaussian with sigma~0.25 m/s, flagged as a guess.
where: project working notes vs research/scripts/measure_tracking_noise.py:21-40 vs research/CORE_PLAN.md:162
why_it_matters: At the noise floor the two kernels agree to within 0.005 (Cauchy 0.900 vs Gaussian 0.895), so the disagreement is invisible exactly where anyone would check it. At 3 sigma they differ by three orders of magnitude (0.100 vs 1.2e-4) -- and the tail is where the whole 'does an uncontrolled machine farm the turning term?' question lives. A cycle could adopt the measured sigma under the wrong kernel and get a reward that pays 85% for no yaw control.
cheapest_next_step: state the kernel explicitly wherever sigma appears, and record the chosen one in the reward spec. The design cycle must pick one and say why; nothing in the repo currently records that a choice was ever made.
resolution: Closed 2026-07-27 by cycle 006's build, and noticed by cycle 007's recall rather than by anyone revisiting this row. The kernel is now stated in all three places the row asked for. (1) research/measurements/tracking_noise.json states it as its FIRST key: 'cauchy: Phi(u) = 1/(1+u^2)', beside floor_score_under_kernel 0.9 and the sigma = 3 * floor rule. (2) The reward spec records it: config.json reward_spec.terms[track_cmd].params carries kernel='cauchy' and frame='heading', and both are inside the reward hash e374eb2def4e6fc9, so a silent kernel swap changes the hash and reward-spec fails. (3) The tracking-frame guard asserts the kernel numerically -- Phi(1)=0.500000 against the Gaussian's 0.367879 -- so the two cannot be confused at the 3-sigma tail where they differ by three orders of magnitude. CORE_PLAN.md:162's Gaussian sigma~0.25 guess was superseded by sigma_v=0.15, sigma_w=0.1 under Cauchy.

what: ent_coef collapses to 4.86e-4 by 52k steps on HoundPDTrackDesert-v0, roughly 37x lower than the 0.0181 the old-reward PD runs held at 1M steps, and it is still falling. ep_len_mean falls monotonically alongside it: 270 -> 232 -> 186 -> 162 over the first 52k steps.

Under the OLD reward this number sat around 0.018 for a whole million steps, so the tracking reward has changed the entropy dynamics substantially and nobody predicted that. It is also the first 3.5% of a 1.5M-step run, where a from-scratch policy falling over constantly is normal, so it is NOT yet evidence of anything.
not_chased_because: The run is live and the pre-registered mid-run gate at 800k steps is what decides whether it is parked. Reacting at 52k would be reacting to the initial transient. docs/theory/command-tracking-reward.md failure mode 5 asks for a SUSTAINED collapse of median episode length below ~400 across the first 300k steps before calling it a spiral.

what: The documented bracketed-pgrep idiom, pgrep -af "bestiary[.]train[.]train", matches the launching shell itself in any cycle that LAUNCHES a run, and reports a spurious second live trainer.
why_it_matters: STATE.md and the run-episode skill both document the brackets as THE fix for pgrep self-matching, with the comment 'brackets, always'. The brackets stop the pattern from matching the pgrep process, but they do not stop it matching a shell whose command line legitimately contains the literal text 'bestiary.train.train' -- which is exactly what a launch command is. Observed twice today: once at launch, once while checking a background greedy_eval. A cycle that trusts the count rather than reading the lines would conclude two runs are live and either refuse to launch or, worse, believe it inherited a run it actually started.
not_chased_because: The correct check already exists and is unambiguous: systemctl --user show robotics-train-<name> -p MainPID --value, plus reading the pgrep OUTPUT rather than counting it. Widening the idiom is a small edit to two documents and belongs in a quiet cycle, not one holding a live run.
evidence: this cycle's launch transcript; the matched line is the bash -c wrapper, not a trainer

what: episodes/004 published 1078.2 as hound_pd_desert_v0's greedy mean at n=60. The same checkpoint measured today with the same tool gives 1049.10 on seeds 0-59 and 1045.76 on seeds 100-159. The 29-point gap to the published figure cannot be reproduced or explained.
why_it_matters: Cycle 006 first explained this as ordinary sampling error, citing a +/-41.8 standard error from seed 0's own spread. That explanation is measured FALSE: block-to-block reproducibility of this instrument on the same checkpoint is 3.34 points, not 29, because the block mean is essentially determined by the crash count and both blocks drew 8 crashes. greedy_eval is byte-for-byte deterministic, verified by repetition, so the tool is not the source. episodes/004 says only 'three disjoint seed blocks' and never records WHICH seeds, so 1078.2 cannot be re-derived from the record at all. A published number in an append-only record that nobody can reproduce is worse than a wrong one, because it will be quoted.
not_chased_because: It needs a seed search over episode 004's possible blocks, or the operator's memory, and neither is cheap while a run is live. The practical damage is already contained: STATE.md, the ledger row and learnings/010 all now carry 1049.10 with its protocol stated, and nothing downstream depends on 1078.2.
candidates: a different seed0 offset (e.g. 3 blocks of 20 at 0/100/200)
a different episode count per block
an earlier checkpoint, before the run's final eval overwrote ant_sac_best.zip
a pre-fix version of greedy_eval or the env

what: ant_sac_best.zip is overwritten in place during a run, so any mid-run measurement of it names an artifact that no longer exists. Cycle 007 hashed it immediately before and after a 20-episode-per-cell track_eval and confirmed it unchanged (42b8ef1d...); it was overwritten 40 minutes later at 11:07:01 (28657a7d..., best single-episode 264.96 -> 497.31) while the refutation of that very measurement was still running.
why_it_matters: Hash-before-and-after is the obvious provenance check and it is insufficient by construction: it proves the artifact was stable DURING the measurement, not that it is retrievable afterwards. Every mid-run number this project takes off _best is therefore unreproducible in principle, which is a stronger defect than learnings/008's selection bias -- that one says the number means the wrong thing, this one says the number cannot be recomputed at all. It bit immediately: the refuter re-measured a DIFFERENT checkpoint under the same filename and only noticed because the sha had moved.
cheapest_next_step: copy the checkpoint to an immutable path before measuring it (runs/<name>/measured/<sha>.zip), or have track_eval/greedy_eval do the copy themselves and record the destination. The copy is 5 MB.
not_chased_because: the final harvest at 1.5M measures both checkpoints after the run is down, where the artifact is stable, so this cycle's headline numbers are unaffected.

what: track_eval.py's own docstring says mean_track 'survives cost-coefficient retuning and episode-length changes'. The second half is false, and it is false in the direction that flatters a crashing policy. mean_track is a per-step score averaged over episodes of unequal length, so a policy whose episodes end at ~720 steps is compared against zero action's 1000. Raw: 0.0955 vs 0.0650, x1.47. Normalised to a common 1000-step horizon: 0.0644 vs 0.0650, ratio 0.992.
why_it_matters: drive_grid_track is the number the record explicitly tells readers to trust when drive_grid_ratio is unreadable because returns go negative -- STATE.md, the cycle 006 note and the run-episode handoff all say 'read drive_grid_track first'. It is the designated safe metric and it carries a length bias nobody documented. Cycle 007 used it to claim the policy beats zero action on tracking; length-normalised it does not, at all.
cheapest_next_step: _arm() already receives per-episode step counts from rollout() and discards them (track_eval.py:129 returns steps, :146-157 drops it). Keep them, report mean_steps per cell, and either normalise mean_track to a fixed horizon or rename it so the per-step-over-unequal-episodes semantics are visible.
resolution: The BIAS is real and is now a guard (track-length-bias, 7 assertions, fast tier) plus three separately-named aggregates in track_eval. The NUMBERS in this row are not reproducible and never will be. Row 20's 0.0955 is measurements/hound_track_desert_s0_midrun_950k.json, measured on ant_sac_best.zip at 950k with 71 crashes; that file was overwritten in place on 2026-07-27 at 11:07:01. Re-measured under the identical protocol today: 0.0718 on ant_sac.zip and 0.0695 on ant_sac_best.zip, against zero action's 0.0650 which reproduces BIT-FOR-BIT (0.06500765521917337), proving the protocol and env did not move. The x1.47 -> x0.992 reversal was therefore a property of one vanished checkpoint's crash rate, not of the metric. Today the bias is +6.9% / +2.4% and length-normalised the policy still marginally WINS (1.032, replicated 1.027 on seeds 5000-5009). Row 20's normalised 0.0644 is permanently unverifiable: the 950k JSON predates mean_steps, track_income and reward_track, so it was hand-derived and cannot be recomputed. research/scripts/track_length_bias_math.py.

what: The pre-registered 'parked in the standing basin' detector cannot flag the null policy it exists to flag. docs/theory/command-tracking-reward.md failure mode 1 calls mean Phi_v < 0.15 on the drive slices 'parked'. Measured over the six drive cells as track_eval's _arm defines them, ZERO ACTION itself reads Phi_v = 0.2399 -- above its own threshold.
why_it_matters: The (0.0, 0.0, 0.45) pure-turn cell has commanded v_x = 0, where a standing machine scores Phi_v = 0.946 for correctly not moving forward. Averaging that cell into a 'is it driving?' detector lets one free cell carry the mean over the threshold. A detector that returns 'not parked' for the do-nothing policy is not a detector, and calibration.jsonl row 13 was written against the same six-cell mean.
cheapest_next_step: define the parked detector over the five cells with nonzero commanded speed, where zero action reads 0.0986, and restate the 0.15 threshold against that denominator. Both numbers are already in tracking_baseline_zero_action.json.

what: track_eval's EVAL_GRID still contains (-0.3, 0.0, 0.0), but commit a4e7ef5 raised VX_MIN_BACKWARD to 0.40, so backward commands are now sampled from |vx| in [0.4, 0.8]. Any policy trained after that commit is scored on a backward command it is never trained on. The forward floor stayed 0.3, so the forward cells are unaffected.
why_it_matters: That one cell is the single worst in the whole record and the only one whose tracking gap is negative BEFORE any cost is subtracted (-0.1383/step at w_ctrl=0). The record cites it as proof that no control-cost coefficient can rescue the reward -- it is quoted that way in STATE.md's ranked next actions and it is the hardest constraint the redesign was told to satisfy. If the cell is off-distribution for every future run, that constraint is partly void, and the drive_grid_mean headline silently becomes one-sixth generalization test.
cheapest_next_step: decide deliberately whether the backward eval cell is an in-distribution score or a generalization probe, and either move it to -0.4 (matching the sampler, breaking comparability with rows 1-4 on that cell) or keep -0.3 and report it separately from the drive-grid mean. Do not change it silently: every published drive_grid number averages it in.

what: The Phi_v x1.46 / Phi_w x0.48 ratio pair is measured on the mid-run ant_sac_best.zip at 950k, while the four-term decomposition printed in the same paragraph is measured on the final ant_sac.zip at 1.5M. On the final checkpoint the same six-cell means are x1.195 and x0.606. Confirmed by research/scripts/two_checkpoints_one_table.py.
where: research/learnings/011, research/episodes/007-*.md and ledger.jsonl row 4 all carry the mixed table; sources are research/measurements/hound_track_desert_s0_{final_sac,midrun_950k}.json
why_it_matters: anomalies row 19 records that ant_sac_best.zip is overwritten in place, so the 950k artifact those two numbers came from no longer exists and they cannot be re-derived from disk. Separately the pair does not compose the way the prose implies: 1.460 x 0.478 = 0.698 while the measured track ratio at that same checkpoint is x1.468, because drive_grid_track is a mean of per-cell products and mean-of-products is not product-of-means (off by 24.1% on the final checkpoint). The cancellation MECHANISM survives on both checkpoints; the specific multipliers and the ratio arithmetic do not.
cheapest_next_step: quote the per-cell delta-track per step instead of arm-mean Phi ratios -- it is what nulls.jsonl row 4's release condition is actually written over, and it is checkpoint-labelled. Do not edit learnings/011 or episode 007: a superseded learning gets a new number and a past episode is never retrofitted.

what: The termination penalty's derivation assumes a contact cost of ~0.045/step for supporting the robot's weight. Measured on a standing machine it is 0.00928/step -- 4.85x smaller. That assumed figure is roughly half of the assumed c = 0.10/step net loss rate that produced TERMINATION_PENALTY = 10.0 = c/(1-gamma), so the input to the formula was already wrong before the achieved-vs-assumed problem arose. Computed by docs/lessons/scripts/006_discounting_math.py.
where: src/bestiary/envs/hound_track.py module docstring (contact cost ~0.045/step) and docs/theory/command-tracking-reward.md failure mode 8, vs research/measurements/hound_track_desert_s0_final_sac.json
why_it_matters: K = c/(1-gamma) prices escaping a negative running stream, so it is only as good as c. The trained policy's measured net rate on the drive grid is -0.00619/step against the assumed -0.10/step, making the shipped penalty 16.2x the stream it exists to cancel. An over-large death penalty is not neutral: it pays the policy to avoid termination rather than to track, which is one candidate explanation for a machine that keeps its feet and stops following commands -- exactly the 950k-to-1.5M trade already in ledger row 4 (crashes 71->7 of 120 while command_gain fell 0.482->0.1935).
cheapest_next_step: re-derive K from a MEASURED early-training net rate rather than an assumed one, and state which policy the rate belongs to. The theory note's own failure mode 8 already flags the inherited contact cost as odd and defers it to a separate commit; this is the number that makes it concrete.

what: track_eval's EVAL_GRID scores the policy on the command (-0.3, 0, 0), but the env's BACKWARD command floor is 0.40. Commit a4e7ef5 raised min |v_cmd| from 0.3 to 0.40 on 2026-07-27 to close the backward freeride, and the EVAL_GRID constant in record/track_eval.py was not moved with it. So one of the six drive cells scores every policy on a command the training distribution never draws.
where: src/bestiary/record/track_eval.py EVAL_GRID cell 3, against the backward floor asserted by guards/check_track_rel.py and by the tracking-frame guard ('env samples |vx| >= 0.3 forward / 0.4 backward')
why_it_matters: One sixth of drive_grid_mean and drive_grid_track is measured off the training manifold. It is not obviously a large error -- the module docstring already refuses to evaluate a policy trained with zero-filled command slots for exactly this reason, and this is a milder version of the same objection -- but it is the same class of mistake. It also biases in a KNOWN direction: -0.3 is the easiest backward command in the grid, and standing's creep is backward at -0.03553 m/s, so this is the cell where a do-nothing machine does relatively best. Zero action's drive_grid_mean of 3.91 is therefore an OVER-estimate of what standing earns on commands the robot is actually trained against, which makes the release condition slightly harder than it needs to be rather than easier -- the safe direction, but not a reason to leave it.
cheapest_next_step: A DECISION, not a patch. Changing EVAL_GRID would break comparability with ledger row 4 and with every published drive_grid_mean, including the 55.73 and 3.91 baselines. The options are (a) leave it and document that cell 3 is off-manifold, (b) add a parallel grid and report both, (c) move it to -0.4 and re-measure both zero-action baselines, accepting that older numbers become unquotable. Do not silently edit the constant.

what: A training session ended at 03:55:05 on 2026-07-28 with roughly 6.7 hours of its working window still open, in the middle of a correction it had already diagnosed. It had killed its own run at 03:50:43 for a real and correct reason, edited two files to fix it, and stopped before committing them, relaunching, or updating any state file. The fix survived only because the next session found the diff uncommitted in the working tree and a single explanatory line in the journal.
where: the systemd journal for the session unit at 03:55, the failed transient unit robotics-train-hound_track_rel_s0, and the uncommitted diff to src/bestiary/envs/hound_track_rel.py recovered at 04:20
why_it_matters: The GPU was cold for 40 minutes and the single most important finding of the window -- that BETA_W = 0.75 paid a standing machine 0.160/step on every turn command -- existed nowhere on disk except as an uncommitted edit. Had that working tree been cleaned, or had the next session trusted the state file instead of checking the machine, the exploit would have shipped into a multi-hour run and the record would have carried a result produced under a reward nobody intended. The state file's own instruction to verify itself against the machine is what caught it.
cheapest_next_step: Find out whether sessions have a duration or resource limit that ends them mid-work. If they do, the obligation to write findings to disk has to be discharged INCREMENTALLY -- commit the fix the moment it is derived, not at the end -- which is a change to how every session is structured rather than a fix to any one of them.

what: The '*_best.zip is overwritten in place mid-run' defect has now destroyed a SECOND measurement, and this time it destroyed a published conclusion rather than an artifact reference. anomalies row 20's headline (x1.47 raw -> x0.992 normalised, 'length-normalised the policy does not beat zero action at all') was measured on a 71-crash ant_sac_best.zip that was overwritten 9 minutes after the measurement was committed. Neither surviving checkpoint reproduces it; both say the policy marginally wins.
why_it_matters: The record's rule is that a number is trustworthy because code computed it from a named artifact. When the artifact is mutable, that guarantee is void RETROACTIVELY and silently -- the JSON still says checkpoint: ant_sac_best.zip and still looks fully sourced. Cycle 007 already recorded this defect and noted that hashing before and after is insufficient by construction; the fix it named (copy to an immutable path before measuring) was never built, and the cost of not building it is now one wrong entry in the record that three later cycles reasoned from.
cheapest_next_step: record/track_eval.py and greedy_eval.py should copy the checkpoint to research/measurements/<name>.<sha256>.zip before rolling it out, and write that path plus the sha256 into the JSON instead of the bare filename. Then a measurement names something that cannot change. A guard can then assert every measurement JSON's checkpoint path still hashes to what it recorded.

what: track_eval's mean_track counted the terminal unhealthy step's Phi, which the env explicitly refuses to pay (hound_track.py:311, 'phi_v*phi_w if healthy else 0.0'). So the naive product over-counted tracking on exactly the crashing episodes the length correction exists to handle. Found by adversarial review of this cycle's own fix, not by the cycle. Magnitude ~8.3e-4 absolute on the crashing cell, 3.6e-5 relative -- immaterial to every conclusion drawn, and wrong.
where: src/bestiary/record/track_eval.py rollout(), fixed 2026-07-28 to source track_income from term_sums['reward_track']
why_it_matters: It is a general pattern rather than one bug: an instrument that RECOMPUTES a reward term from its ingredients will drift from the term the env actually paid the moment the env adds a condition to it. The env's own info dict is the only authority on what was paid. Two other places may have the same shape -- greedy_eval and the training callbacks -- and neither has been checked.
cheapest_next_step: Audit every place a metric recomputes a reward quantity instead of reading it from info. Then assert, on one real rollout, that the summed info terms equal the summed reward -- the env already residualises to 2.8e-14, so the assertion is cheap and would have caught this.

what: Content-addressed checkpoint freezing (record/freeze.py) covers exactly TWO of at least SIX code paths that load a checkpoint and can produce a number that reaches the record. Unwired: research/scripts/heading_ceiling.py:190, research/scripts/track_return_decomposition.py:102, research/scripts/deterministic_vs_stochastic.py:337, research/scripts/policy_lesson_math.py:23, and src/bestiary/train/watch.py:64. Three of those four scripts WROTE the very measurement JSONs now grandfathered in guards/measurement_provenance.py.
why_it_matters: Cycle 011 was about to record that this failure class is now 'impossible'. It is not: it is optional in two of six paths. The ad-hoc research script is the path that actually produced the numbers in anomalies rows 18/20/23, so the covered paths are not the ones with the track record of causing the problem. watch.py is benign (it renders, it does not publish a number); the four scripts are not.
cheapest_next_step: Have the research scripts call record.freeze.freeze_checkpoint too, or -- better, because it needs no discipline -- move checkpoint loading behind one helper that freezes, and make loading a checkpoint any other way the thing that is hard to do.

what: NOTHING forces a measurement to be written to research/measurements/ at all. track_eval.py:411 and greedy_eval.py:344,350 only print to stdout; a number reaches an episode or a learning by copy-paste. measurement-provenance can only police files that exist, so a cycle that quotes a number without saving its JSON is invisible to the guard and always will be.
where: src/bestiary/record/track_eval.py, greedy_eval.py (stdout only); the guard reads research/measurements/
why_it_matters: This is the actual mechanism of anomalies 20/23/27, and freezing does not touch it. The freeze makes a SAVED measurement durable; it does nothing about an UNSAVED one, and the unsaved one is the common case because saving is a manual step a tired cycle skips. Cycle 010 additionally committed a 0-byte measurement file and quoted a number out of it, so 'a file exists' is not sufficient either.
cheapest_next_step: Make the tools write the JSON themselves rather than print it -- a measurement that is not on disk should be the hard path, not the default one. Then a guard can assert every number quoted in an episode traces to a committed file.

what: measurement-provenance passes when the frozen checkpoint it should verify is ABSENT (guards/measurement_provenance.py, the 'not present locally' branch). Since runs/ and *.zip are gitignored, deleting runs/<name>/measured/ silently converts any future MISMATCH into a PASS. On the repo today the assertion verifies 0 artifacts and is green.
why_it_matters: It is a deliberate trade and it is still a hole. Failing on absence would make the guard fail for everyone who clones Bestiary, since no frozen copy ever travels with the repo; passing on absence means the guard's strength depends on files nobody is required to keep. The honest reading is that this guard detects CORRUPTION of a retained artifact, and does not and cannot guarantee RETENTION.
cheapest_next_step: Decide whether frozen checkpoints are retained deliberately (a retention policy in SYSTEM.md, and a guard asserting the frozen copies named by committed measurements still exist on THIS machine) or accepted as best-effort. Do not silently rely on it either way.

what: The privacy guard's dollar-figure rule fires on LaTeX. Any dollar sign followed by a digit matches, so display math opening with a numeral and inline values like a gamma of 0.9 written in maths delimiters both FAIL as suspected currency. Hit three times in one cycle (learnings/014 once, docs/lessons/009 twice) as the lessons got more mathematical -- and a FOURTH time on the first draft of this very row, which quoted currency examples to illustrate the rule and was correctly rejected for it.
why_it_matters: It is a false positive in a guard whose failures must never be waved through, and that combination is corrosive: the guard that must be obeyed most is becoming the one most often wrong, on the files this project writes most. The danger is the habit, not the friction -- four rejections in one cycle is how a loop learns to reach for the allowlist, and this is the one guard where a wrongly allowlisted line cannot be walked back once pushed. Every instance so far was fixed by rewriting prose, never by weakening the rule. That is the correct direction and is not guaranteed to survive time pressure.
cheapest_next_step: Teach the rule to skip maths spans (text between single and double dollar delimiters) rather than growing an allowlist, and require a currency match to carry a separator or a magnitude word rather than merely a leading digit. Do NOT relax it without the span rule: the current behaviour is wrong in the safe direction, and the fourth rejection above proves the rule still catches real figures.

what: A commit landed in this cycle with a FAILING privacy guard, because the shell line was 'guards --fast 2>&1 | tail -2 && git add ... && git commit'. A pipeline's exit status is its LAST command's, so tail always returned 0 and the guard's verdict gated nothing. The guard had failed, the failure was printed, and the commit proceeded anyway.
where: the cycle's own shell usage. CLAUDE.md documents the correct idiom, 'guards --fast || exit 1', which is not what got typed
why_it_matters: Same shape as learnings/014 and anomalies row 30: a check that runs, prints, and gates nothing is indistinguishable from a check that passed. Here the failure text was even on screen, hidden by a tail -2 showing only a summary line. The repo already knows this class from the other end -- CLAUDE.md records that sourcing the venv makes the documented guard line exit 127 and report a failure that never ran. Piping the guard is the same defect wearing different clothes, and it took ONE cycle after writing a learning about vacuous checks to commit one.
cheapest_next_step: Never pipe the guard invocation that gates an action: run it bare with '|| exit 1', or capture to a file and test the status separately. A pre-commit hook makes it structural rather than remembered; install-hooks.sh exists and its --check is already on the carried list.

what: checkpoint_width.py:299-309 has three different sets in play in one finding. Label 'every run records the observation spec it trained against' quantifies over all 13 runs and read literally is FALSE for 10 of them; ok is hardcoded True; n=len(pinned)=3 counts only the runs satisfying the predicate; and the detail's subject is the other 10. The aggregate n ruling (count the checkable set, exclude the uncheckable remainder) does not rescue it: the 10 unpinned runs are not UNCHECKABLE for this predicate - 'does this config carry an obs_spec key' was asked of all 13 and answered no for 10. They are counterexamples, not unknowns, so n counts the passing subset, which is the one thing n must never be.
why_it_matters: A finding that cannot go red no matter how the number moves is the learnings/014 failure in a second form: not vacuous, but unfalsifiable. Two honest shapes exist and both are behaviour changes an operator should see: rename to 'runs predating the obs-spec record are declared, not back-filled' with n=len(unpinned), matching the sibling wording already in terrain_spec.py:312 and reward_spec.py:175; or keep the universal label and let ok = not unpinned, which turns it red today.
not_chased_because: cycle 012 was auditing the suite, not editing its verdicts, and either fix changes what a published guard asserts. Found by the refutation of 012's own claim.

what: The guard suite's total 'verified' count is not stable while a run is live. guard_vacuity.py reported 6955, then 6956 during the refutation, then 6995 - all within one cycle, with no code change between the last two. The mover is runs/hound_track_rel_s1, which is being written to as the audit reads: disk.py's n=len(finished) EXCLUDES the live run while metric_liveness's n=len(scalars) grows with it as more scalars are logged.
why_it_matters: Any coverage number quoted from this script is a single draw from a moving state, not a property of the repository. A later cycle comparing 'verified' across two dates would read training activity as a change in guard coverage. The vacuity COUNT was stable at 3 throughout, so the headline survived - but only because vacuity is a threshold at zero and the totals are not.
not_chased_because: the cycle's claim was about the vacuity count, which did not move. Freezing the audit against a quiescent machine, or recording the live-run set alongside the total, is 013+ work.

what: `guards --fast --json` raised `TypeError: Object of type bool is not JSON serializable` while all 13 fast guards reported green in plain text. Cause: tracking_frame.py builds a Finding whose `ok` came from a numpy array comparison, so it is `numpy.bool_`, not `bool`. It is truthy, prints as `True`, and satisfies `if finding.ok` identically; it differs in exactly one place, json.dumps -- which reports the name of the builtin it is NOT, making the message actively misleading.
why_it_matters: The machine-readable output is what the record consumes; it was dead from tracking_frame.py's first commit (2026-07-27T07:56) until 2026-07-28, roughly two days, and NOTHING in the suite could see it because the plain-text path never serialises. This is a guard suite that could not check itself. It is also learnings/014's shape in a new place: green did not mean checked.
not_chased_because: chased and fixed in this cycle. Coerced in `Finding.__post_init__` (bool for ok, int for n, None left as None) rather than at the one producing site, so a future guard comparing two arrays cannot reintroduce it. Regression catcher `guards.check_finding` added, 7 hermetic assertions, verified to report 5 of 7 FAILED with the coercion reverted.
found_by: incidental, by an Opus 5 subagent auditing guard birth dates for an unrelated question

what: Cycle 012 proposed that guard vacuity is a function of a guard's AGE. Measured across all 16 guards (record.guard_birth_audit), the proposal survives but the MECHANISM is wrong. Of the 11 testable guards, 5 were born vacuous and 6 born covering, and the split is not by age -- the whole suite spans 51 hours, so age barely varies. It splits by WHAT THE SET IS: all 6 born-covering guards quantify over a category that already existed (runs/, ledger rows, nulls rows); all 5 born-vacuous guards quantify over a FIELD THE GUARD ITSELF INVENTED (obs_spec, reward_spec, terrain_spec, best_eval_episodes, a measurement sha256). Vacuity duration is latency to the next producing event: the two long gaps (25.5 h, 27.4 h) both waited on a training run, the short ones (1.0-2.8 h) landed in the same cycle as one. Positive gaps median 2.80 h, range 1.02-27.36 h.
why_it_matters: It changes what the loop should DO about vacuity. Under the age model, waiting fixes it and nothing is owed. Under the field-invention model, a guard that demands a new field is vacuous until a PRODUCER is wired, which is a task with an owner, not weather -- and it predicts which guards will be born vacuous BEFORE they ship. It also weakens the reassurance cycle 012 took from `measurement-provenance` being merely young: at 1.7 h it sits below the whole observed band, so its 3 vacuous assertions are not yet evidence either way.
not_chased_because: the data cannot settle it and this cycle's experiment was the harvest. n=11, one repository, 51 hours of guard history, and 5 of the 5 supporting points are RECONSTRUCTED rather than observed -- `n` did not exist as a field until cycle 011, so no one ever saw checkpoint-width render VACUOUS. One of the 3 live vacuous assertions also resists the model outright: it is empty because of a hand-written grandfathering constant, which is an authored decision rather than accumulation.
falsifier: The model dies if a guard stays vacuous while data of its declared type accumulates. Concretely: if >=3 new measurement JSONs naming checkpoints are written after 2026-07-28T06:25 and measurement-provenance is STILL vacuous, emptiness is design rather than shipping latency. The observed band gives a hard deadline of 2026-07-29T10:00 (max gap 27.36 h). Symmetrically, a new field-inventing guard that ships born NON-vacuous also breaks it.
found_by: Opus 5 subagent, cycle 013, sent to confirm the age model and returning a better one

what: Anomaly 33's remaining half: `install-hooks.sh --check` existed, was correct, and included a probe that proves the prepare-commit-msg hook FIRES rather than merely exists -- and nothing ever called it. Cycle preflight went from nine checks to ten; the check now runs as 4a and both repos report `ok` and `fires` today.

A backstop nobody invokes reports nothing, which is the same failure shape that let five attributed commits reach the public repo on 2026-07-27 while the installer said green because the hook sat in a directory git ignores (core.hooksPath).

what: track_eval's reward decomposition is INCOMPLETE and looks complete. Its TERMS tuple is hardcoded to four terms (track, ctrl, contact, termination), but HoundPDTrackRelDesert-v0's config.json carries a fifth, pbrs_shaping (weight 1.0, gamma 0.99, cauchy potential). The four reported terms do not sum to the reported return: residual -0.78 on the zero-action arm (20 PERCENT of its 3.91 baseline), -1.19 on ant_sac_best, -1.25 on ant_sac. Found by the cycle-013 refuter, not by the instrument.
why_it_matters: This is exactly the learnings/014 shape - an instrument reporting a complete-looking accounting of an incomplete set. Row 4's whole conclusion was a decomposition argument (ctrl cost = 102.9 percent of the gap), so a silently-missing term is the failure mode that would have corrupted it.
fix_not_taken: Derive TERMS from the env's own RewardSpec instead of a hardcoded tuple, and assert the terms sum to the return within tolerance. Then a new reward term cannot fall out of every future decomposition unnoticed. This is a guard, not a patch.

what: command_gain has no yaw twin. It regresses achieved FORWARD velocity on commanded, so it is structurally blind to yaw - the exact axis where this policy is dead (mean_phi_w 0.141/0.178/0.040 on the three yaw-commanded cells against zero action's 0.969). The cycle pre-registered command_gain as its lie-detector against a command-independent gait and set the bar at 0.05; the policy scored 0.382 while ignoring yaw entirely.
why_it_matters: A pre-registered falsifier that cannot see the failure it was written to catch is worse than none, because it returns a pass.
fix_not_taken: Add yaw_gain: achieved yaw rate regressed on commanded across the yaw-commanded cells. It would have read ~0 here.

what: The disk guard and record.retention disagree for ~30 minutes after every run finishes. retention holds a 30-minute grace before pruning a finished run's replay buffer ('buffer written 25 min ago -> SKIP'), but the disk guard fails immediately once the ledger row exists ('no finished run is still holding a replay buffer: 1 run(s), 2.6 GB recoverable'). Observed at 10:25 on hound_track_rel_s1, whose row was appended at ~10:05.
why_it_matters: guards --fast GATES EVERY TRAINING LAUNCH. So for half an hour after a run lands and is harvested - exactly the moment a cycle would launch the next seed - the launch gate is red for a reason that is not a problem and that the recommended remedy explicitly refuses to fix. A cycle under time pressure meeting this either waits, or does the dangerous thing and bypasses the gate.
fix_not_taken: Either the disk guard should honour the same grace as retention, or retention's grace should not apply once a ledger row exists (the row is the signal the buffer is no longer needed). The second is better: the grace exists to protect a still-resumable run, and a run with a ledger row is finished by definition.
